title: Long QQQ — Conditional CPI Relief Tactical; Entry Only on SPX EOD Close Above 7,460
entry: CONDITIONAL — do NOT initiate this position unless SPX closes above 7,460 today (June 10). Enter on the close or in the last 10 minutes of the session if SPX is tracking above 7,460. Scale: 100% at the conditional trigger; no add-ons. If ORCL RPO guidance disappoints after the close tonight ($553B flat or below), exit the entire position on Thursday's open regardless of SPX level — the ORCL binary eliminates the AI re-rating thesis that justifies the entry. Position must not be held through SPCX pricing on Thursday June 11 without an explicit reassessment.
stop_loss: SPX daily close below 7,380 on any session while this position is held — implies the CPI relief faded intraday and the HOLD regime did not confirm, meaning the gap-open that fades is distribution (per the prior brief framework's explicit warning). The stop is index-level, not QQQ price-level, because this is a macro regime trade, not a technical trade on QQQ's chart.
targets: $725 — reclaim the June 9 close zone ($730) and the pre-Iran-escalation morning bounce; SPX confirmation above 7,460 persists through Thursday; +2.6% from QQQ $706.67 entry

$742 — approach the prior all-time high zone at $748.65 (the 52-week high from June 2); ORCL RPO beat ($600B+) drives enterprise AI re-rating overnight; broad semi-sector lift adds to the QQQ move; +5.0%
$750 — blue sky; SPX closes above 7,500, completing the HOLD → BUY upgrade; VIX closes below 16; Iran escalation fails to materially disrupt markets; QQQ reclaims the ATH zone; +6.1%
risk_reward: 1:3.5 to third target (from $706.67 entry if condition fires)
catalyst: May CPI printed below the 4.2% YoY consensus this morning, triggering the morning briefing's STEP ASIDE → HOLD upgrade and restoring macro tailwinds for Nasdaq 100 growth names. The prior QQQ short (short-qqq-fade-nq-bounce-cpi-2026-06-08) was positioned for a hot CPI print; Target 1 was hit at $706.67 today as Iran-driven session selling reinforced the directional move despite the CPI relief. After covering the short, the morning brief establishes a conditional tactical long: the SPX close above 7,460 is the only signal that confirms the CPI relief has converted from a bounce into a regime upgrade. At $706.67, QQQ is 3.2% below the prior short entry and nearly 6% below the June 2 all-time high — the conditional risk/reward is constructive only if the regime threshold clears.
thesis:
The conditional entry structure is not timidity — it is regime discipline. The morning briefing's explicit framework states: 'a gap-open that fades is distribution.' May CPI printing below consensus is a necessary but not sufficient condition for a Nasdaq tactical long. If SPX closes above 7,460 today, it means the post-CPI bounce has been sustained through a full session of Iran escalation headlines, SPCX positioning flows, and ORCL uncertainty — a close above the regime floor under those headwinds represents a genuine regime clearing event that justifies a tactical position. If SPX fails to close above 7,460, the condition is not met and no position is initiated.

The macro backdrop for this trade is the most constructive since the June 5 regime breakdown. Three of five regime indicators have cleared: DXY estimated below 100 (~99.05), Brent below $97 (~$91.96), and 30Y below 5.0% (~4.93%). The two remaining in breach — VIX (~18.10, at the trigger) and SPX (~7,438, 22 points below the 7,460 floor) — are both measurably improving. A single session of SPX above 7,460 combined with VIX below 17 would clear four of five indicators simultaneously, triggering an automatic HOLD → BUY upgrade per the briefing framework. A QQQ long entered on that signal captures the regime upgrade in real-time.

The ORCL binary is the primary overnight risk management consideration. ORCL reports Q4 FY2026 at 5 PM EDT today — the $553B RPO backlog and $19.10B revenue / $1.96 EPS consensus create a binary with a market-implied range of +/−10.63% for ORCL, with spillover effects across cloud and AI infrastructure names including QQQ. The conditional entry structure accommodates this: if SPX closes above 7,460, the entry fires; if ORCL then misses RPO guidance, the position exits on Thursday's open regardless of the stop level. This makes the trade a maximum one-session hold with a binary overnight event.

The counter-party is the investor who argues: QQQ at $706.67 after the short worked means the CPI-driven relief has already been partially sold; entering a long after covering a short on the same ticker within 24 hours is confirmation bias. The SPCX $75B pricing Thursday June 11 creates guaranteed institutional sell-side flows that weigh on QQQ components at the exact moment the tactical long is exposed. And if ORCL disappoints, the long absorbs the overnight gap. These are all valid objections — which is why the position is sized at 2%, the entry is conditional, and the exit on an ORCL miss is mandatory and automatic.
bull_case: SPX closes above 7,462 today (condition fires). ORCL beats — RPO guidance above $600B. QQQ opens Thursday at $720-725 on ORCL beat. VIX compresses below 17 on Thursday. SPCX pricing absorbs with less disruption than feared. QQQ extends toward the prior ATH at $748 within the week.
bear_case: SPX condition does not fire (position never initiated — clean exit, no loss). OR condition fires on SPX $7,461 close, ORCL misses RPO guidance ($550B or below), QQQ opens Thursday at $685-695, stop triggered via SPX 7,380 breach on Iran headline. Maximum loss on 2% position: approximately 3–4% loss if entered near $706 and stopped at a QQQ corresponding to SPX 7,380.
invalidation: Entry condition not met: SPX fails to close above 7,460 today (position never initiated). OR ORCL Q4 FY2026 RPO guidance disappoints (exit Thursday morning open regardless of price). OR SPX closes below 7,380 on any session while held.
